findings.reason: the section's sole deliverable is gated by a control that fires a third of the time with nothing wrong, so the control must be restated as §8's point-estimate threshold (line 108) or at a run count where a percentile interval has power before a node can execute it.
findings.text: §12's negative control asks that two pseudo-arms of the ~4-run baseline local arm give overlapping 90% bootstrap intervals on cumulative input per run; at two runs per pseudo-arm the percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean is exactly that pair's own [min,max], so on a perfectly homogeneous population the two intervals are disjoint in 2 of the 6 possible 2/2 splits — one chance in three — and the record must then declare the population too noisy and withhold the figures the section exists to report

findings.reason: §8's metric list does include input per run and the section draws no verdict, so nothing is misdirected; aligning the statistic would sharpen the control without changing what a node does.
findings.text: the control is stated on cumulative input per run, while §8's adoption metric — and §8's own parity control at line 108 — use cumulative input per landed node against a 5% threshold; overlapping intervals at two runs per arm pass halves that differ by far more than 5%, so the control sets no noise floor for the statistic the record's comparison rests on
